questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Assess how pupils can share, adapt and preserve cultural practices respectfully.
questions.prompt: A pupil wants to share a family greeting at a class cultural display. What should the group do first?
questions.answer: Ask the pupil to explain when the greeting is used.
options: Ask the pupil to explain when the greeting is used.
Assume it is used the same way everywhere.
Ask the pupil to replace it with the most common greeting.
Use it as a joke to get the audience’s attention.
questions.explanation: Asking the pupil to explain the context helps the group present it accurately.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Assess how pupils can share, adapt and preserve cultural practices respectfully.
questions.prompt: A drama group borrows a storytelling technique from another country but keeps the local story and its ending. What does this show?
questions.answer: A group can adopt a technique while preserving parts of its own tradition.
options: A local story becomes foreign whenever its performance changes.
The borrowed technique replaces the story’s message.
Keeping the ending prevents the group from learning anything new.
A group can adopt a technique while preserving parts of its own tradition.
questions.explanation: The performance technique changes, while the local story and ending are retained.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Assess how pupils can share, adapt and preserve cultural practices respectfully.
questions.prompt: Two classes want to make recordings of community stories. Which plan best supports respectful preservation?
questions.answer: Ask storytellers for permission and record their names and the setting of each story.
options: Collect as many clips as possible and remove details about where they came from.
Ask one pupil to retell every story from memory and list them all as originals.
Ask storytellers for permission and record their names and the setting of each story.
Publish the recordings first and ask storytellers about permission later.
questions.explanation: Permission respects the storytellers, while names and context help listeners understand the records.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Assess how pupils can share, adapt and preserve cultural practices respectfully.
questions.prompt: What does it mean to respect cultural diversity at a school event?
questions.answer: Give different groups space to explain their traditions in their own words.
options: Expect every group to present the same custom.
Give different groups space to explain their traditions in their own words.
Assume each group’s traditions are identical within every community.
Rank groups by the number of pupils who already know their customs.
questions.explanation: Respect includes listening to how people describe their own practices.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain and apply self-control and responsible habits in school situations.
questions.answer: Following an agreed study plan even when nobody is watching.
options: Working only when a teacher stands beside you.
Following an agreed study plan even when nobody is watching.
Finishing early by copying someone else’s work.
Waiting for another pupil to organise your books each day.
questions.explanation: Self-discipline involves managing your own behaviour without constant supervision.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain and apply self-control and responsible habits in school situations.
questions.prompt: During a group activity, Chidi feels angry after his suggestion is rejected. What response shows self-control?
questions.answer: Pause, then ask why the group preferred another suggestion.
options: Pause, then ask why the group preferred another suggestion.
Interrupt until the group changes its choice.
Agree aloud and hide the group’s materials afterwards.
Decide that the group must restart the activity before anyone explains.
questions.explanation: Pausing and asking a question helps Chidi respond without disrupting the group.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain and apply self-control and responsible habits in school situations.
questions.prompt: A class makes a rule to return shared scissors to one tray. Pupils follow it, but the tray is locked during lessons. Why do delays continue?
questions.answer: Pupils still cannot reach the equipment when they need it.
options: The rule prevents pupils from returning the scissors.
The class needs a different place for every pair of scissors.
Pupils must have ignored the rule.
Pupils still cannot reach the equipment when they need it.
questions.explanation: The return routine solves where equipment is stored, but the lock prevents timely access.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain and apply self-control and responsible habits in school situations.
questions.prompt: A team keeps forgetting its cleanup duty. Which plan makes responsibility easiest to check fairly?
questions.answer: Make a rota with named duties and check the work together before leaving.
options: Ask everyone to help but leave the tasks unassigned.
Give all duties to the pupil who complained last.
Make a rota with named duties and check the work together before leaving.
Change duties after the work is done so nobody can plan ahead.
questions.explanation: The rota assigns duties clearly and a shared check shows what still needs doing.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Choose considerate actions and reason about effects on neighbours.
questions.prompt: A family plans a celebration in a shared compound. What can they do to help neighbours prepare?
questions.answer: Tell neighbours the expected time and keep the shared walkway clear.
options: Send an invitation without mentioning when the event will end.
Move neighbours’ belongings from the walkway without asking.
Tell neighbours the expected time and keep the shared walkway clear.
Tell neighbours after the celebration has begun.
questions.explanation: Advance notice and clear access reduce disruption for others.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Choose considerate actions and reason about effects on neighbours.
questions.prompt: Two households agree to share a water tap. A dispute starts when both need it before work. Which change addresses the cause most directly?
questions.answer: Agree on a morning schedule that gives each household a turn.
options: Clean the tap at the end of the week.
Agree on a morning schedule that gives each household a turn.
Add a sign explaining who installed the tap.
Ask both households to bring larger buckets.
questions.explanation: The disagreement is over access at the same time. Scheduling turns addresses that conflict.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Choose considerate actions and reason about effects on neighbours.
questions.prompt: A neighbour says a leaking container in the shared corridor is harmless because it belongs to them. Which reason best challenges that claim?
questions.answer: The water can affect everyone who walks through the corridor.
options: The water can affect everyone who walks through the corridor.
The container is useful only when it is carried outside.
A shared corridor makes every object inside it jointly owned.
People should never store water in containers.
questions.explanation: Ownership does not remove the consequences for others using a shared space.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Choose considerate actions and reason about effects on neighbours.
questions.prompt: Why is it helpful to offer a specific kind of help to a neighbour carrying groceries?
questions.answer: The neighbour can decide whether that help is useful and accept or decline it.
options: The offer means the neighbour must hand over their bags.
Offering help gives you the right to choose where the groceries go.
The neighbour will be unable to carry anything without help.
The neighbour can decide whether that help is useful and accept or decline it.
questions.explanation: A clear offer respects the neighbour’s choice and avoids assumptions about what they need.
